full_judgment:
2. The respondent Md. Akramuddin, a Telephone Revenue Inspector, approached the administrative Tribunal, Dhaka with an application marked as Administrative Tribunal Case No. 139 of 1993 under section 4 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 for a direction to the petitioner for payment of his arrear salaries and allowances. The said Tribunal, by an order dated 26 April 1997, allowed the prayer. Being aggrieved the petitioner filed Appeal No. 91 of 1997 before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka, but it was out of time by 60 days. In order to get over the bar of limitation the petitioner filed therewith an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act seeking condonation of the delay. 

 3. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal, by its order dated 19 March 1998, dismissed the appeal as time barred with the observation inter alia that section 5 of the Limitation Act had no manner of application for condonation of delay in filing appeal before the said Tribunal. 

 4. in view of the fact that the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 is a special law and the provision of section 5 of the Limitation Act has not been made applicable to an appeal before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal the learned counsel for the petitioner has hardly any ground to assail the impugned order of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal.
